A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CausalToM and lookback-mechanism study. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original activation-patching, subspace-intervention, attention-knockout, and correlation experiments, including evaluations on CausalToM and BigToM.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a behavioral model survey, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct interventions, and three-triple CausalToM experiments.

M1.justification: The binding, answer, and visibility lookbacks, causal-intervention methodology, DCM procedure, and Algorithm 2 remain unchanged. The additional models and three-triple experiments test the existing mechanism rather than introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix O adds CausalToM scenarios involving three characters, objects, and states under both visibility conditions. Mechanistic evaluation covers the new no-visibility scenario. The original two-triple CausalToM and BigToM coverage is retained.

E2.justification: No alternative belief-tracking or interpretability method is newly evaluated against the proposed causal explanation. Table 1 surveys language models as experimental subjects for model selection; the existing full-residual versus DCM-subspace comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds FP32 Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct to the mechanistic evaluation and documents a behavioral survey of 15 model configurations using 100 samples per run. Appendix N uses 80 counterfactual pairs and full-residual interventions. The retained experiments' sampling and DCM training protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices N and O substantially extend tests of mechanism generalization across model families and increased entity complexity. New Qwen experiments include source-freezing controls and localization of binding and answer components; three-triple tests additionally expose failure under visibility. Existing knockout and correlation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports means and standard deviations over 10 independent runs of 100 samples each. This explicit uncertainty reporting concerns behavioral model selection; v3 does not establish additional repetitions or changed statistical treatment for the retained causal-intervention plots.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds behavioral accuracies, including Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct means of 0.962 without visibility and 0.912 with visibility. Appendices N and O add layerwise intervention results and report inconsistent three-triple visibility performance in all three tested models. The original Llama and BigToM result curves are retained, rather than improved or replaced.

T1.justification: The causal-abstraction formalism, Equations 1–10, and Algorithm 2 are unchanged. New Appendix C supplies standard residual-stream and attention equations explaining concepts already used, without introducing a new theoretical assumption, derivation, or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central contributions: CausalToM and belief tracking through binding, answer, and visibility lookbacks. Adding Qwen to the introduction and extending the experiments supplies further evidence without redefining these main claims.

C2.justification: Appendix O newly identifies three-triple visibility as an applicability boundary and restricts causal validation there to no visibility. Appendix N explicitly interprets the evidence as generalization across model families. Section 9 also adds a proposed role for internal analysis in detecting deception and persuasion, without experimentally demonstrating that application.

D1.justification: v3 specifies Qwen's FP32 precision and discloses two 80GB NVIDIA A100 GPUs for local Llama-70B and Qwen experiments. Section 10 gives more specific model-hosting and NDIF reproduction information. The code/data access address and existing DCM hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 7 substantially expands research positioning: it adds a strand on methods for improving ToM, explicitly distinguishes that goal from explaining existing mechanisms, and replaces short citation lists with individual discussions of binding and belief-representation studies. References are added, including Sclar et al. (2023), Wilf et al. (2024), and Yang et al. (2025), while several earlier probing and steering references are removed.

P1.justification: Substantial explanatory revision is concentrated in rewritten related-work and ethics sections and the new five-part background Appendix C. Section 3 gains numbered subsections, and the appendices accommodate new background and evaluation sections. The central mechanism exposition remains largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 enlarges key mechanism diagrams, adds a structured behavioral table and 17 experimental figures, and interleaves retained Llama-405B figures with corresponding Qwen figures. Original graphics remain present, although their placement, sizing, and some captions change.

improvement.justification: Table 1 quantifies previously qualitative model-selection claims, while Qwen and three-triple interventions strengthen generalization evidence and disclose a visibility failure boundary. Background explanations and hardware details improve accessibility and reproducibility. These gains remain limited by the unresolved visibility-payload interpretation and qualitative reporting of three-triple behavioral performance; new Figure 43 also contains an inconsistent example answer.
